Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
waxm...@gmail.com wrote:
> Can you play a Unique master, then contest with yourself and yield?
>
> I'm sure this is answered in the rulebook, but I'm a moron.

No. You cannot volluntarily play a copy of a Unique card that you
already control. There are ways to play a second copy of a card you
control already involuntarily (Vast Wealth, influencing vampires), in
which case you burn the new copy immediately and do not contest with
yourself. But you can't contest your own cards voluntarily.

-Peter

Yes. To spite us all, they put it in the hard to find section 4.1,
"Contested Cards".

Be careful about putting duplicates of the same unique cards in
your deck. You can't control more than one of the same unique
card at a time, and you cannot contest cards with yourself (if
some effect would force you to contest a card with yourself,
then you simply burn the incoming copy of the unique card). On
the other hand, you may wish to have a second copy handy in case
the first is burned

Frankly, I think it's an outrage that such an important piece of text
should be clearly and intelligently written in a well-marked section of
the rulebook. It's clearly a double-bluff to make us all ignore it.

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:


Re-read the rule: "you cannot contest cards with yourself". Not
'titles', 'cards'.

A political title is not a card, therefore you can contest your own
title (unintentionally or otherwise). And the cards that provide titles
(like Nos Justicar) are neither unique nor typically stay in play, so
there's no issue about contesting those, either.

-John Flournoy
